lineage: Windows locker reuses leaked Conti v2/v3 code; 2023 Linux/ESXi encryptor largely rewritten (~29% similarity)
summary: Monti emerged in mid-2022 as a near 'doppelganger' of Conti, reusing leaked Conti code and tradecraft. BlackBerry's IR case showed initial access via Log4Shell against an internet-facing VMware Horizon server, tools pulled down with Chrome, Action1 and AnyDesk RMM for persistence, LSASS dumping/Mimikatz, a Veeam credential dumper, RDP and PsExec lateral movement and exfiltration to MEGA, before encrypting desktops and an ESXi cluster (.PUUUK). Trend Micro reported a reworked Linux/ESXi encryptor in 2023 focused on legal and government sectors.
uniqueTraits: Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) against VMware Horizon Connection Broker for initial access
Action1 cloud RMM abuse (first reported in a ransomware intrusion) alongside AnyDesk
Exfiltration of the LSASS dump to DropMeFiles and bulk data to MEGA/MEGASync
Conti-clone Windows locker (.PUUUK) plus ESXi encryptor with soft VM shutdown, --whitelist option and /etc/motd ransom note

chain.procedure: Conti-derived Windows locker encrypted 18 desktops and a 3-host ESXi cluster (21 servers), appending .PUUUK with a Conti-style note; the 2023 Linux variant uses AES-256-CTR with size-based partial encryption.
Linux variant replaces /etc/motd and index.html contents with the ransom note.
